newFindings.title: A caught pre-dispatch cancellation failure can commit a request while leaving the intent dispatchable
newFindings.description: For a pre-dispatch intent, cancellation inserts the durable request and only then sets terminal state. There is no method-local savepoint or rollback-only mark. If the second operation fails and the trusted transaction callback catches the error and returns, the surrounding transaction can commit the inserted request without cancelling the intent. Claims and checkpoints do not consult the request table, so that intent remains dispatchable.
newFindings.reproduction: Using the unchanged production includes transpiled in memory and real SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT, enqueue a pending intent. Inject a PersistenceFault at delivery.claim.state after the request INSERT but before its UPDATE. Await cancel_delivery_intent inside the transaction, catch that fault in the callback, and let the outer transaction commit. Read the intent and request, then run a new claim and possible-dispatch checkpoint.
newFindings.impact: The durable cancellation request and terminal cancellation state can diverge after a recovered method fault. This is a private callback/error-atomicity gap, not evidence of a successful cancellation result being falsely returned, public authorization bypass, an actual provider send or automatic replay after possible dispatch.
newFindings.callerCondition: The normal path remains safe if every cancellation error propagates and rolls back the surrounding transaction. The failure requires catch-and-commit; current conditional live-token/await requirements alone do not forbid that awaited recovery pattern. A caller contract explicitly enforcing rollback after cancellation failure could bound approval, but no such enforced guarantee was observed.
newFindings.requestedCorrection: Make the pre-dispatch request and terminal transition atomic even if the caller catches a storage failure, using the supported transaction/savepoint mechanism or enforced rollback-only behavior. Add a focused test that fails the state write, catches the method error inside the callback and commits/attempts to commit; no unmatched pre-dispatch cancellation request may survive while the intent remains dispatchable. Keep post-dispatch request-only behavior, budgets, identity and FIFO unchanged.
newFindings.acceptance: Independent re-review of corrected cancellation bytes and the caught-failure regression. A successful later cancellation and its request must commit together; post-checkpoint/unknown cancellation still must not mark cancelled or release FIFO.
newFindings.scopeLimit: The injected failure is a deterministic adapter failure before the terminal SQL callback, with the real database and compatible schema. This is not a reproduced native PostgreSQL failure; server-aborting PostgreSQL errors may prevent the same catch-and-commit path. The shared method also lacks local atomicity for non-server/pre-execution errors. No SQLite corruption, migration or authorization claim is needed for the demonstrated private callback path.

positiveAssessments: The live transaction requirement is checked at method entry and through the unchanged guarded executor. Empty identity is rejected; missing intent returns missing; succeeded/failed/cancelled return terminal without reopening state.

lockIntent acquires the same job/ordering-key write lock used by claim/checkpoint/renewal, re-reads the intent after locking and keeps it in the caller transaction. At supported isolation, cancel-first blocks checkpoint, while checkpoint-first records a request without asserting rollback.

Pending/retry_wait and running before possible_dispatch become cancelled on normal completion. State gates reject stale claim/checkpoint/renewal afterward, retain the existing ledger/count/fence/deadlines and permit later same-key work.

After possible_dispatch=1 or a consistent outcome_unknown state, cancellation returns requested and does not touch intent state or any ledger fields. Lease-expiry unknown and later-key FIFO remain blocked.

The request table has one primary-key row per intent and an FK to the delivery row; the timestamp is authoritative database UTC. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING retains the first timestamp across repeated requests.

Inconsistent pending/retry_wait with a possible marker, unknown without a possible marker and running/unknown missing ledgers fail closed. Fresh compatible stored schema remains an explicit assumption.

Positive method results inside callbacks are provisional. The inspected rollback tests and independent probes show that outer rollback removes request/state changes and, on first use, the lazy cancellation-table DDL.
No authored/public/operator endpoint, provider call, authentication decision, receipt claim or worker/scheduler binding is introduced by the reviewed cancellation method.

inspectedThreeTests.limit: Rollback tests throw out of the surrounding transaction after a positive method result.
